## The same data can be long or wide

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| label: long
long <- tibble(
  geo = c("a", "a", "b", "b"),
  var = c("x", "y", "x", "y"),
  val = c(5, 6, 7, 8))
long
```
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| label: wide
wide <- long |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = var,
              values_from = val)
wide
```
:::
::::

Long: one row per place **and** variable. Wide: one row per place.

## pivot_longer() reverses it

```{r}
#| label: longer
wide |> pivot_longer(cols = c(x, y), names_to = "var", values_to = "val")
```

## Practice: renter shares from long data

`data/renter_l.rds` has two rows per municipality: renter households and total households.

```{r}
#| label: renter-l
renter_l <- read_rds("data/renter_l.rds")
renter_l |> head(4)
```

Compute the renter share for each municipality and sort from the highest.

## Answer

::: {.small}
```{r include=params$answers}
#| label: renter-answer
renter_l |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = vector, values_from = value) |>
  rename(renters = contains("Renter"), households = contains("Total")) |>
  mutate(renter_share = renters / households) |>
  arrange(desc(renter_share)) |>
  head(5)
```
:::

## Duplicate keys break pivot_wider()

::: {.small}
```{r}
#| label: dup-pivot
#| warning: true
long_dup <- long |> add_row(geo = "a", var = "x", val = 9)
long_dup |> pivot_wider(names_from = var, values_from = val)
```
:::

::: {.warning}
Two values for `a`/`x` produce a list column. Check first: `count(geo, var) |> filter(n > 1)`.
:::

## Practice: price index from wide data

`data/pindex_w.rds` has one row per CMA and one column per month of a new housing price index.

```{r}
#| label: pindex
pindex_w <- read_rds("data/pindex_w.rds")
dim(pindex_w)
```

Make it long, turn the month names into dates with `ym()`, and plot one line per CMA.

## Answer

::: {.small}
```{r include=params$answers}
#| label: pindex-answer
#| fig-height: 3.2
pindex_w |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -GEO, names_to = "month", values_to = "index") |>
  mutate(month = ym(month)) |>
  ggplot(aes(month, index, colour = GEO)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "New housing price index", colour = NULL)
```
:::

## Joins combine tables by a key

```{r}
#| label: bands
band_members
band_instruments
```

## inner_join() and left_join()

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| label: inner
band_members |>
  inner_join(band_instruments,
             by = "name")
```

Only names in both tables.
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| label: left
band_members |>
  left_join(band_instruments,
            by = "name")
```

Every row of the left table.
:::
::::

## right_join() and full_join()

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| label: right
band_members |>
  right_join(band_instruments,
             by = "name")
```

Every row of the right table.
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| label: full
band_members |>
  full_join(band_instruments,
            by = "name")
```

Every row of both tables.
:::
::::

## Keys with different names

```{r}
#| label: by-different
band_instruments2
band_members |> left_join(band_instruments2, by = join_by(name == artist))
```

## Check the row count after every join

```{r}
#| label: dup-join
extra <- band_instruments |> add_row(name = "John", plays = "piano")

nrow(band_members)
band_members |> left_join(extra, by = "name") |> nrow()
```

One duplicate key in `extra` added a row. Make R check for you:

```{r}
#| label: relationship
band_members |> left_join(extra, by = "name", relationship = "many-to-one")
```

## Find the rows that did not match

```{r}
#| label: anti
band_members |> anti_join(band_instruments, by = "name")
```

`anti_join()` returns the rows of the left table with no match on the right. Mick has no instrument recorded.

## Names make poor keys

```{r}
#| label: names
renter_l |>
  distinct(`Region Name`) |>
  filter(str_detect(`Region Name`, "Langley"))
```

Two municipalities share the name "Langley". Join on codes such as `GeoUID` whenever you can.

## Application: life satisfaction by province

```{r}
#| label: health
health <- cansim::get_cansim("13-10-0905-01") |>
  filter(REF_DATE == "2024", GEO != "Canada (excluding territories)",
         Indicators == "Life satisfaction, satisfied or very satisfied",
         `Age group` == "18 to 34 years", Sex == "Both sexes",
         Characteristics == "Percent") |>
  select(GeoUID, GEO, satisfied = VALUE)
nrow(health)
```

## Join it to census data by GeoUID

::: {.small}
```{r}
#| label: health-join
provinces <- cancensus::get_census("CA21", regions = list(C = "01"), level = "PR") |>
  select(GeoUID, province = `Region Name`, Population)

provinces |> left_join(health, by = "GeoUID", relationship = "one-to-one") |> nrow()
provinces |> anti_join(health, by = "GeoUID") |> select(province)
```
:::

The survey does not cover the territories, so they get `NA`. Say so in your caption.
